item.title: The Harrowing Survival Tale Of The 11-Year-Old Girl Who Was Orphaned At Sea
item.description: Known as the "Sea Waif," Terry Jo Duperrault spent more than three days adrift at sea until she was found. The post The Harrowing Survival Tale Of The 11-Year-Old Girl Who Was Orphaned At Sea appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Archaeologists Have Uncovered A Siberian Ice Mummy Who Underwent Jaw Surgery 2,500 Years Ago
item.description: Members of the ancient Pazyryk culture of Central Asia drilled two holes in a woman's injured jawbone and threaded it together with hair or tendon to create a "primitive prosthetic" circa 500 B.C.E. The post Archaeologists Have Uncovered A Siberian Ice Mummy Who Underwent Jaw Surgery 2,500 Years Ago appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: The Fascinating Story Of The Remote Island Lodge Known As The ‘Loneliest House In The World’
item.description: Built in 1953 as a hunting lodge, the "world's loneliest house" is located on an island five miles south of Iceland that's inhabited only by puffins. The post The Fascinating Story Of The Remote Island Lodge Known As The ‘Loneliest House In The World’ appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: John Haigh, The ‘Acid Bath Killer’ Who Dissolved His Victims In Vats Of Sulfuric Acid
item.description: Between 1944 and 1949, British serial killer John George Haigh murdered at least six people, destroyed their remains in acid, and stole their assets. The post John Haigh, The ‘Acid Bath Killer’ Who Dissolved His Victims In Vats Of Sulfuric Acid appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: The Gruesome Reason Why Chainsaws Were Invented
item.description: The chainsaw was invented to more safely perform a brutal surgery known as a symphysiotomy on laboring women, during which the birth canal was widened with a hand-cranked, rotating blade. The post The Gruesome Reason Why Chainsaws Were Invented appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: The Skeletal Remains Of 18 Nazi Soldiers Were Found In A Mass Grave In Poland
item.description: Among the dead were weapons, tools, a pocket watch, and a medal of honor for fighting in the Spanish Civil War. The post The Skeletal Remains Of 18 Nazi Soldiers Were Found In A Mass Grave In Poland appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Inside The Troubled Marriage Of Johnny Cash And Vivian Liberto
item.description: Vivian Liberto was Johnny Cash's first wife and had four children with him. But after their divorce in 1967, she was cast as the bitter shrew who held his talents back. item.title: The Secretive Life Of Albert Francis Brown, The Son Of Al Capone
item.description: From an early age, Albert Francis "Sonny" Capone struggled under the weight of his father's last name. So he decided to change it — then disappeared to California. The post The Secretive Life Of Albert Francis Brown, The Son Of Al Capone appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: The Wreck Of A Luxury Steamer That Sank In 1872 Has Been Found Intact And Upright On The Bottom Of Lake Michigan
item.description: The Lac La Belle sank off the coast of Wisconsin due to inclement weather more than 150 years ago — and it's taken shipwreck hunters decades to finally locate it. item.title: Inside The Remarkable Story Of Jack Johnson, The First Black Heavyweight Champion
item.description: Known as the "Galveston Giant," Jack Johnson made history as the first African American to hold the world heavyweight boxing championship. The post Inside The Remarkable Story Of Jack Johnson, The First Black Heavyweight Champion appeared first on All That's Interesting.
